nodes.summary: The Scottish Book Problem 7 claim is false: there are a real Banach space $E$ and closed convex subsets $A, B \subseteq E$, each with infinite-dimensional linear span, that are not homeomorphic.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 7 fails: closed convex sets need not be homeomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space and let $S = \{x \in E : \|x\| = 1\}$ be its unit sphere. Then there is a continuous map $f : E \to E$ such that $f(x) \in S$ for every $x \in E$ and $f(x) = x$ for every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Retraction onto the unit sphere of Hilbert space

nodes.summary: For a real inner product space $E$, the statement that the projective Hilbert space of $E$, the unit sphere $\{x \in E : \|x\| = 1\}$ with each $x$ identified with $-x$ and given the quotient topology, is homeomorphic to $E$.
nodes.title: Projective Hilbert space homeomorphic to the space itself

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space. Then the projective Hilbert space of $E$, the unit sphere $\{x \in E : \|x\| = 1\}$ with each $x$ identified with $-x$ and given the quotient topology, is not homeomorphic to $E$.
nodes.title: Projective Hilbert space is not homeomorphic to Hilbert space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed additive commutative group, in practice a real inner product space. The projective Hilbert space of $E$ is the quotient of the unit sphere $\{x \in E : \|x\| = 1\}$ by the relation identifying each $x$ with $-x$. Its points are the antipodal pairs $\{x, -x\}$ of unit vectors, that is, the diameters of the unit sphere.
nodes.title: Projective Hilbert space

nodes.summary: Ulam's claim that for every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space $H$ with unit sphere $S = \{p \in H : \|p\| = 1\}$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, all continuous functions $f_1, \dots, f_n : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and every continuous map $T : S \to S$, there is a point $p_0 \in S$ with $f_i(T(p_0)) = f_i(p_0)$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 167

nodes.summary: The claim that in every real Banach space $E$, any two closed convex subsets $A, B \subseteq E$ whose linear spans are infinite-dimensional are homeomorphic, with the subspace topologies.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 7 (Mazur–Banach)

nodes.summary: Ulam's claim in Problem 167 is false: there are an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space $H$ with unit sphere $S$, a number $n \in \mathbb{N}$, continuous functions $f_1, \dots, f_n : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and a continuous map $T : S \to S$ such that no point $p_0 \in S$ satisfies $f_i(T(p_0)) = f_i(p_0)$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Negative answer to Scottish Book Problem 167
